hook_text: Same data, two graphs, and one of them is lying. Can you spot which?
clip_script: Fruit survey in Mbombela. Apple 9, banana 7, orange 5, mango 8, grapes 3. Pictograph: one apple picture for each learner, all the same size, lined up. Nine apples, seven bananas. Easy to count. Now a bar graph: fruits along the bottom, numbers up the side, starting at 0 in equal steps. Apple bar to 9, grapes bar to 3. Fair. Now the liar: scale starting at 3. The grapes bar vanishes and apple looks huge. Same data, wrong story. Start at 0, equal steps, same-width bars, and a title and labels. Then your graph tells the truth.
visual_style: Whiteboard pictograph of fruit in neat rows; a bar graph drawn with a ruler; a second, misleading bar graph with a cut-off scale flashing red.
pacing: Fair pictograph, fair bar graph, the lying graph reveal, then the checklist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw a bar graph of the books your family reads this month.
